precepts.text: Here is the reality check for the evil sisters who think, if I am evil he must be evil, we will just be evil together. I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. A man will be delivered from a woman like that. So do not think you can just stay evil and you two will be together forever; the Lord will deliver him. How about you just repent and get it together so you can be heirs together.
precepts.point: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun. Which he hath given thee: brothers, the Lord gave her to you. That sister was created for you. This is your portion all the days of your life.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
Here is the reality check for the evil sisters who think, well, if I'm evil, he's evil, we're just going to be evil together. Solomon says: “And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”.

Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. A man will be delivered from that type of woman. He will escape; he will get away.

So, sisters, don't think you can just be evil and die that way and the two of you will be together forever. No. The Lord will deliver him. How about we just repent and get our stuff together, so you can be heirs together? The wife the Lord gave is meant to be lived with joyfully all the days of your life, as a portion, not as a snare.

precepts.text: If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, give her a bill of divorce, and let her go. This is the worldly marriage of a man trying to repent whose wife keeps the traps going. It is not the biblical marriage: once married in this truth she is yours for life unless she commits adultery, and there is no divorce in the Bible.
precepts.point: Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her, because she was his portion and was meant to destroy him. Some are not made to make it; if your spirit is not girded, one of these temptations takes you.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
“whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.” A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man. But what about the man who complains of a wicked woman and claims he is not wicked himself? If that is true, he will find a way to escape. Sirach shows the way: “If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.”

This is the brother in the world trying to repent, trying to get his house in order and straighten it out, while his wife keeps up the traps of Ecclesiastes 7:26: her heart snares and nets, her hands as bands, creating chaos and assignments so he can't get to camp, to the brothers, to the meetings. She doesn't want to listen. Then let her go. And it goes both ways; it is about you men too.

But understand: this is not talking about a biblical marriage. Once you get married in this truth, she is yours for life, unless she commits adultery. There is no divorce in the Bible, and we don't dissolve marriages up in here; it is written in our rules. This is for those coming in from outside this truth, with all kinds of situations.

So the man who pleases God escapes from her. But if you allow yourself to be destroyed, you were indeed wicked, and the woman sent to you was your portion for real.

precepts.text: If the unbelieving depart, let him depart; a brother or sister is not under bondage in such cases, but God hath called us to peace. The bondage is the worldly marriage. When the spouse says I want nothing to do with that Bible and keeps the pork on one side of the stove, let them go. Those coming out of such situations have work to do before remarrying, and leadership holds the records; lean back when told to, because every backdoor marriage story is worse than the last.
precepts.point: Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her, because she was his portion and was meant to destroy him. Some are not made to make it; if your spirit is not girded, one of these temptations takes you.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Paul speaks to the same case: “But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace.”

The man was wicked and inherited a wicked woman. Why? God orchestrated it, to see whether he would stay there, and to reflect what is in us so that we can change. The Lord is interested in the elect, so he puts us through trials and temptations to see if we will overcome them.

The bondage is the worldly marriage. When the spouse says, I don't care what you do, I want nothing to do with that Bible, and makes it plain and won't bend, still cooking pork and ham hocks on one side of the stove, this half is for you since you're keeping those laws, we're going to keep eating chitlins and hog maws, the house smelling like butt: if the unbelieving depart, let them depart. That is the woman of Ecclesiastes 7:26 whose heart is traps and nets, and whoso pleases God shall escape.

But those coming out of these situations have a lot of work to do before they can even think about properly marrying, and brothers and sisters are impatient. Leadership are the fathers of the men and women, and we have the records. When we tell you to lean back and let the brother or sister work on themselves, it is for a good reason, because the backdoor marriage stories are horrible, and they get worse every time a new one pops up.

precepts.text: Wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, that if any obey not the word they may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives, while they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. A sister at a Passover panel asked when she could leave a husband of ten years who had followed her through Africanism and Islam; to him this truth is one more fad until he sees it is real. Come home disciplined, not cursing him out, dressed properly, and tell him you want him to take command. If he is righteous he comes in behind you; the same goes for a brother who repented last week and wants to turn the house upside down this week. Many wives have said, I did not know he was this serious, he was willing to let me go, and came in. The timetable is the Lord's, not your hormones.
precepts.point: Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her, because she was his portion and was meant to destroy him. Some are not made to make it; if your spirit is not girded, one of these temptations takes you.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Before anyone walks away, look at the other side. At a Passover panel years ago a sister asked when she could walk away from her husband in the world. They had been together about ten years, through Africanism, through Islam, through different things. In his mind this truth might be just another fad. Wait, sister. Lean back.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” He is worldly, but he isn't telling you to break the laws of God, so still deal with him properly. Chaste means with discipline: you aren't cursing him out. He watches the change in you, sees the fear of the Lord in you, and sees it is serious, not a phase.

“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, “the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.” She puts on proper clothing, and tells him: my husband, I want you to come in and take command, so I can deal with you as a proper wife. He comes home from catching hell at work and she knows how to pull him out of it, and he asks, where are you learning this wisdom? If he is righteous, he comes in behind you; we have seen it many times.

Men do the same: a brother who was in sin with his wife last week wants to turn the house upside down this week. Give her a chance to see you're serious. Wives have said, I didn't know he was this serious; he was willing to let me go, and they came in behind him. That is the Most High giving righteousness to righteousness.

precepts.text: Wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence.
precepts.point: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Looking means acting when a brother struggles.

note.label: The Highway of the Upright: an Israelites's Strait Journey

precepts.why:
Looking on the things of others means building something together, and economics must be part of our mindset as we walk to build a nation. Solomon says: “For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.”

Wisdom is a defence: generational wisdom passed down from father to son, grandfather to son. Esau has law in his house, and the grandfather passes the torch and teaches hard lessons that save heartache; that is why they had the head start, and why they are so relaxed at their jobs. We are behind in everything. Half of black folks have a credit score below 620, locked out of access to capital; before we wake up in the morning, half of us are in bondage.

Money is a defence. Walking the commandments, evil is going to come upon you: what happens when they take your job? So build businesses we can self-employ in, food distribution, brothers helping each other. Teach your children about secured loans and secured credit cards and the three credit bureaus, Experian, TransUnion and Equifax. And a single, divorced brother paying out his money has less of a defence than a man married in proper order.

“wisdom giveth life to them that have it”, and to have it you have to be taught it. That is why they try to stop us from teaching that we are the twelve tribes of Israel: scattered, we lost our nationality, heritage and commandments. The father in the house, with Christ at his head, is the one to break that cycle.

precepts.text: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad.
precepts.point: Thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see. Racial anger at oppression is in the scriptures; those who feel nothing have shut down.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
Oppression makes a wise man mad. That is racial anger, and it is in the scriptures. Deuteronomy 28:33 gives the oppression: “The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours, shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”. That is what was told of the man brought to this side of the world. Then verse 34: “So that thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.”

You are going to be mad. Your eyes are going to be mad for what you see: the oppression, all the evil taking place against your people. You see your wife being raped and you cannot do anything. You see your people being lynched and you cannot do anything. You are just angry. The curse prophesied that anger.

So if you see your people oppressed and going through these things, and you are not mad, not angry, something is not right. You have shut down. There must be racial anger. Being mad at the sight of the oppression of our people is not a sin to be ashamed of; it is what the scripture said the oppression would do to us, and it is the wise response to what our eyes have seen.

precepts.text: Do not say the former days were better; know the history as it was.
precepts.point: An Angolan man given as a present is the fulfilment of nations sending gifts one to another.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another”. Esau rejoiced over our downfall and made merry, as in Merry Christmas. We always thought, we were the gifts, and the history shows it: when Count Frederick von Hanau acquired a large part of what is now Suriname from the Dutch West India Company, he also received as a gift an Angolan man. They sent us around as gifts. Our sons, our daughters, our mothers and fathers were the gifts, because the two prophets, the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel, tormented them; we didn't play with Esau.

The Ecclesiastes called for at this moment is Solomon's word: “I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.” See that right there. The young Black Israelites in those European paintings were supposed to be the princes over Spain and Portugal, and they became servants to the white man: children snatched from their mothers, baptized and made slaves, holding the umbrella, the mirror, tending the horses and cattle.

So when you go into museums in America, France and England and see a picture of a little Black boy holding an umbrella, don't say, oh, look at that cute little Black boy. Now you know the history as it was: those were their slaves, the Moors, the Black Jews of Spain and Portugal, separated from their parents and given a limited education so they could be dumbed down. Princes walking as servants, and nations making merry and sending them one to another as gifts.

precepts.text: Oppression maketh a wise man mad, and a gift destroyeth the heart.
precepts.point: Leaving the world makes you a target, so fulfil your course and do not fall out.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey”. The brothers and sisters who depart from evil, keep the laws of God, repent and come back make themselves a target. The ones comfortable in this captivity have their citizenship here; they fully support this demonic system. Why aren't they a target? Solomon shows how they were bought: “Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.”

Surely oppression makes a wise man mad. Does seeing your brothers and sisters in bondage in captivity not make you men mad? So the gift is how they keep the wise from getting mad. It's like the movie Trick Baby: get hold of the ones with the smarts, the understanding and the education first, so they don't go back and cause an uprising among the people. Give them gifts, good jobs, the desires of their heart, the top-of-the-line jobs, so they feel they're not oppressed, and let them know they cannot go back and help heal their communities.

Once you are fully invested in Esau's kingdom, it's a wrap; they have all the hooks. We're not racist; we gave you a good-paying job and a good education; you were able to buy your mom that house. And you are blinded to the oppression of your nation. Then Satan says it's go time. Trump revoked Executive Order 11246 and the affirmative action and DEI orders: I'm doing away with all of that, I'm going to press the hell out of y'all niggas. The highly educated independent woman with the good job, your ass got to go too. A lot of brothers and sisters got fired behind this demon, because they loved the world and received the gift; serving the white man was their pleasure.

Now he shows his fangs. What are you going to do now? The gift destroyed the heart; the one who departs from evil and takes the target on his back has his citizenship in the kingdom.

precepts.text: The woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her, as Joseph escaped.
precepts.point: The scriptures warn of that spirit: the woman whose heart is snares and nets and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter, and her ways are moveable; the same mouth that flattered turns and accuses.

note.label: Genesis 39: Joseph in Potiphar's House

precepts.why:
“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.” Potiphar’s wife was that woman. Her heart was snares and nets, laid day by day, and her hands were bands: she caught him by his garment.

Joseph pleased God, and he escaped from her. She was left with his garment in her hand, and the sinner would have been taken; but he fled. Then the same woman turned and lied, crying that “he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us”, and laid up his garment by her as evidence until his lord came home. That is the spirit the scriptures warn of.

precepts.text: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof; the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.” Joseph began sold into slavery and put in prison under false pretenses. The end of the thing was governor of Egypt, a father to Pharaoh, with wagons sent to carry his father down. Better is the end than the beginning.

And he got there patient in spirit, not proud in spirit. The patient in spirit is better; that is what carried him from the beginning of the thing to its end.

precepts.text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider; the Most High set the one over against the other.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.” The Most High set the day of prosperity over against the day of adversity; Joseph had both, and Jacob had both, his heart fainting and then his spirit reviving at the sight of the wagons.

In the day of adversity consider the days that were good, and be patient in spirit. Consider means read the Bible more, study more, pray more, apply more. That is what the day of adversity is for.

precepts.text: A gift destroyeth the heart, which is why Hezekiah let his enemies in and showed them everything he owned.
precepts.point: Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in Isaiah 39.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

precepts.why:
“Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.”

Berodach-baladan king of Babylon “sent letters and a present unto Hezekiah.” The gift did its work. “Hezekiah hearkened unto them, and shewed them all the house of his precious things”, the silver, gold, spices, precious ointment and all his armour: “there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah shewed them not.”

A gift destroyeth the heart. Because of the present, Hezekiah trusted his enemies and let them in to see everything he owned, and that is why Isaiah declared it would all be carried into Babylon.

precepts.text: The bitter woman whose heart is snares and nets; the man who pleases the Most High escapes her.
precepts.point: Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and instruments gave thanks because his mercy endureth forever, and all the people departed, and David returned to bless his house.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.”

That is the bitter woman whose heart is snares and nets. When David returned to bless his house, Michal met him with scorn for playing before the Most High. But David had pleased the Most High, and the man who pleases the Most High escapes her.

precepts.text: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men in the city.
precepts.point: Teaching the Law had a real effect on the nations; wisdom disarmed his enemies.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.”

Teaching the law had a real effect on the nations. After the book of the law went through the cities of Judah, “the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.” Wisdom strengthened Judah more than mighty men could.

precepts.text: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools; all our lives we heard the songs of fools.
precepts.point: This "sing a new song" is repeated in Psalm 95, Psalm 96, and Psalm 98. All our lives we have been hearing the songs of fools, R&B, hip hop, and fake gospel. We never sang about the so-called black, Hispanic, and native Indian Israelites taking back over the earth; the Lord keeps reminding us to sing a new song unto Him.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
“It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.” All our lives we have been hearing the songs of fools: R&B, hip hop and fake gospel. We never sang about the so-called black, Hispanic and native Indian Israelites taking back over the earth.

That is why the Lord keeps reminding us, in Psalm 95, Psalm 96 and here in Psalm 98, to sing a new song unto him. He has done marvellous things, and his right hand and his holy arm have gotten him the victory; leave the song of fools and sing about that.

precepts.text: A just man falls seven times and rises up again, so a fall does not undo the righteous man.
precepts.point: Take no heed to all the words that are spoken, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee, for thine own heart knows that thou hast likewise cursed others.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 7: A Good Name and the House of Mourning

precepts.why:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” A fall does not undo the righteous man: he rises up again.

That is how to read “there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.” Verse 20 is one of those verses the Christians love to pull out, the same as the New Testament saying we all fall short and Proverbs saying a just man falls seven times. It does not excuse sin; it shows that no man is sinless. The just man falls and rises up again, while the wicked fall into mischief.

precepts.text: All have sinned and come short of the glory of the Most High, the same point Solomon makes here.
precepts.point: Take no heed to all the words that are spoken, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee, for thine own heart knows that thou hast likewise cursed others.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 7: A Good Name and the House of Mourning

precepts.why:
“For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God”. That is the same point Solomon makes: “there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.”

Verse 20 is one of those verses the Christians love to pull out, the same as this one. It does not excuse sin; it shows that no man is sinless. All have sinned, and a just man falls seven times, but he rises up again.

precepts.text: Oppression makes a wise man mad, and a gift destroyeth the heart.
precepts.point: We honor the Most High with our lips, but when the oppressor offers gifts we turn away and serve our oppressor's will. When Sennacherib's servant Rabshakeh offered Hezekiah two thousand horses, it was the same trick, a gift to pull the heart off the Most High.

note.label: Isaiah 31: Egypt Is Flesh, Not Spirit

precepts.why:
“Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many”, but “look not unto the Holy One of Israel”. How does a people come to that? “Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.”

We honor the Most High with our lips, but when the oppressor offers gifts we turn away and serve our oppressor’s will. Oppression makes a wise man mad, and a gift destroyeth the heart. When Sennacherib’s servant Rabshakeh offered Hezekiah two thousand horses, it was the same trick, a gift to pull the heart off the Most High. The horses and chariots of Egypt are that gift, and trusting in them is the destroyed heart.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

precepts.why: “It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise” than “the song of fools.” Ain't nothing wrong with glorifying the Lord with good righteous music. We have righteous music in Original Royalty. But gospel music singing to Satan, songs to Cesare Borgia, songs full of emotion and feelings that don't bring our people back to who they are—that song is worthless.

points: My thing is — I know it is going to sound like I am stirring things up, but how do black men feel? I got to get real for a second. How do black men feel knowing that somebody that they probably used to run around the neighbourhood with when she was a kid — Tasia Fortune — that she was hung up in the back of an abandoned house to the point where maggots exploded in her body? She had been hung for three days. The decomposition of her body went to that extreme.

Now give me that: oppression making the wise man mad. Because somebody might say I am trying to start something, because I know we are quick to go burn up something, we are quick to go start a riot. I ain't talking about none of that at all. What I am talking about is you organising and getting with your nation and coming underneath the Bible, where it tells us how to gather ourselves together. O nation not desired.

Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad. How does the oppression rest with us, knowing that my sister was hung up there like that, and just left her body to be swinging in the southern breeze, and I know for three days? You mean to tell me none of us saw it? Think about it. This goes back to what Officer Carmela was saying. They saw it, but they were so afraid that if anybody even talked about it they say, master going to come and get me. That is that fear.

And a gift destroyeth the heart. And a gift — Thanksgiving destroyed your heart. The Fourth of July destroyed your heart. So-called Christmas that ain't got nothing to do with Jesus Christ. Jesus was not born in December at all. And he weren't no white man. And the Christmas tree ain't got nothing to do with Christ. So why do we forget? They allow us to participate in pagan holidays and you will forget that your sister was just lynched a month ago.

So, surely oppression maketh a wise man mad. Mad enough to organise, mad enough to come together, mad enough to put down the crack, to put down the dope, put down the alcohol, put down the OnlyFans and the pornography, put all that garbage away and stand up and be real men and organise the way the Most High told us to organise, up underneath his commandments. That is what our sisters need. They need to see that. That is what our brothers need to see. And when we come to your town, they are standing in awe. They cannot believe it. Especially Esau. He really cannot believe it.

note.label: The Pit and Pendulum: The Slow Genocide of the Undesired

points: What will the living do? And the living will lay it to his heart. So why is the Lord allowing brothers and sisters to be given death unto death? So that the living, us alive, will lay it to heart. Meaning we'll have it at the forefront of our minds. As another Nolan Wells happen, we'll lay it to mind and say, damn, we really transgressed against God. As another Sandra Bland, we'll lay it to heart, because we're in the house of mourning now. Correct?

So as we're in the house of mourning, we'll start to lay it to heart. We'll be like, damn, we really have pissed God off. So therefore, when you lay it to heart, both those in the truth and outside — when we are in the truth, you'll no longer teach like a dead fish. You'll be that lively stone on the street to stir up the spirits of our people. You won't be the Visine dry-eyes guy. You going to teach with fire, because you want our people to be stirred up in their minds and to repent.

So we'll lay it to heart each time we hear about these things, these atrocities, and our people will lay it to heart and begin to ask, what is our transgression? What is our sin? How did we offend God so much that all of these things has happened to us?

note.label: Strange Fruit

points: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this. Do not sit back thinking about how everything was good with the ex: the bathwater was ready, the food was always ready. Well, you should have stayed with her. But she did not believe in God and did not want to keep the commandments, so you left and found a woman that believes she is an Israelite, that keeps the commandments and has the faith of Jesus Christ. And now you are comparing her to a wicked woman.

It is the children of Israel in the wilderness: 40 years marching around because they kept looking back at Egypt. We were slaves, but the food was good. The manna even tasted how they wanted it to taste, and they still were not happy; they wanted meat, and when the Most High gave them so much quail they could not take it, they complained again. They kept looking back at their worst condition while the Most High was trying to free them. That is us with the exes in the past. That was not a good situation; you were unequally yoked with a nonbeliever. Now you have a believer, so build her up, teach her, raise her in the scriptures. If you keep going back to how stuff was before, how are you encouraging her to be godly?

Video played in class, a preacher making the point: we treat strangers better than we treat those that we love. We will be rude, disrespectful, mean, cutting, thoughtless, and hateful to those that love us, because we can get away with it. We will give a stranger a compliment, but when was the last time you told your spouse how great they are, how well they are doing, how good they look?

With brothers we do it: bro, I see you, I can tell you have been studying. A brother cuts his hair and lines his beard up and it is a whole celebration in the school. But your wife sits in the salon chair for eight hours, comes home, and asks, can you tell I cut it? And you say, I don't know, yeah, it looks good. We compliment men on their hair more than we compliment our wives on theirs.

points: Oppression maketh a wise man mad, and we are an oppressed people; that we are not mad shows how few wise men we have, except the remnant the Lord saved.

Because we are too comfortable, affliction will increase; in their affliction they will seek me early, and a car, a house and a good job are not going to last.

note.label: Woe to Amerikkka

points: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad. When you see injustice, if you are a wise man it is going to make you angry. The teacher got up angry putting this lesson together. Use the wisdom of God to help your people come out of that oppression: go even harder to teach your people and show them what they have to do to change so these injustices stop. We are not joining any civil rights movement and marching with them; we show our people the solutions.

And we have to be honest about ourselves: the culture our people created here perpetuates violence, music about killing each other and selling drugs to each other, and you know who is behind that: it keeps the prisons full. Our people do not commit the most crime, but we are the only ones who glorify it. We have to change our people's minds and change the way they look at us.

note.label: Seeking Justice in an Unjust System

points: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad. When you're being oppressed, it makes you mad; but you got to direct that anger in the right place, and the right place is the colonizer.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

points: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools. The bitter spirit resides in the bosom of foolish brothers and sisters.

Bitterness has a progression: it starts with correction or an offense; then pride comes in and you do not want to speak to the brother, and when you do speak, you speak in deceit, masking envy, anger, hatred. Ultimately it leads to your destruction and the destruction of those around you.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Solomon said, one man among a thousand have I found, but a woman among all those have I not found. Why? He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and they were idolaters; not one of that thousand sought to serve the Lord. Women are prone to idolatry and easily drawn toward any sinful act; that is why they need a man to say, not that way, go this way.

Then she asked the man, why did the Iran hostage crisis take place? He said religious jihadis hate our way of life. She answered: or they overthrew the Shah of Iran, whom we imposed on Iran because the Dulles brothers, one at the CIA and one at the State Department, decided the oil beneath the soil of Iran belonged to BP and to us. When Mosaddegh, the democratically elected leader, said we would like to audit BP to see if you are cheating us, they said you may not, and then we overthrew him and he died in prison. The hatred of the United States had to do with the hatred of the Shah, who brutally repressed the people of Iran for 26 years until he was overthrown from within. The bottom line is the arrogance of United States foreign policy; we act as if nothing we do has ever led to the hatred of us in other countries. She was on point; give her a hand.

The documentary went on to Gaddafi's end in 2011: NATO drones and French jets struck his convoy near Sirte, he was found hiding in a drainage pipe, and he was beaten and killed by a mob without trial. Summarized in one line: it was the same pattern as Patrice Lumumba in the Congo, paid rebels put on the back of a truck the man who stood up for his people. All of that happened under the Obama administration with Hillary Clinton at State, and the clip of her laughing was played: "We came, we saw, he died."
